title: The Loose Extraction
premise: Noor Lockridge, a veteran crash investigator haunted by the deaths of their family aboard Flight 447, is pulled into a black-ops extraction when a commercial airliner's records are erased mid-flight—aboard it, a defector carrying proof that the crash that killed Noor's family was engineered. Teaming with a disgraced air marshal and the defector's estranged daughter, Noor must smuggle the man out of a hostile country while dodging the syndicate that owns the skies' secrets. The defector turns out to be bait in a trap meant to bury Noor too, forcing them to choose between exposing the truth and saving their found family. In the end, Noor trades their own anonymity—broadcasting the evidence at devastating personal cost—and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Lior Yarrow is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reviewing accident reports before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people who dig through wreckage for answers no one wants found.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Opening on the anniversary of the crash, Noor inspects another airline disaster site, counting rows out of habit until they reach twelve. A colleague notices the ritual; Noor deflects. Emotional beat: grief as routine, the wound that organizes an entire life.

chapters.title: Ghost on the Scope
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A radar technician friend shows Noor an anomaly: Flight 2211's transponder and passenger manifest vanished mid-flight over the Caspian corridor. Officially, the flight never existed. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into dread—the impossible made bureaucratic.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Boarded
chapters.summary: Air marshal Dane Okonkwo's POV. Dane, grounded after a scandal, is approached by a handler offering redemption: extract defector Emil Vasari from Tbilisi before the syndicate erases him like the flight. Emotional beat: a broken man handed one last purpose he doesn't trust.

chapters.title: Manifest of One
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Digging into 2211, Noor finds a single name that survived the purge: Vasari's, flagged by the same shell company tied to their family's crash. Emotional beat: the cold shock of coincidence becoming pattern—the past reaching through paperwork.

chapters.title: Tbilisi Rain
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. Dane lands under cover as an insurance adjuster and makes contact with Vasari, who refuses to move without his daughter Mara, estranged and living in Lisbon. Emotional beat: paranoia and tenderness in equal measure—a man who trusts no one but still loves.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Hung Up
chapters.summary: Mara's POV introduced. Mara, a cargo pilot, gets a call from the father she hasn't spoken to in nine years; she hangs up, then can't stop thinking about it. Emotional beat: resentment braided with longing, the cost of surviving a difficult family.

chapters.title: Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: syndicate fixer Ilse Brandt confirms Vasari has copied the Ledger—the flight manifests proving engineered crashes—and orders the extraction team itself compromised. Emotional beat: chilling administrative evil, murder as logistics.

chapters.title: Recruitment
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Dane appears at Noor's door with the 2211 file, asking for help reading the wreckage data embedded in Vasari's copy. Noor recognizes the flight profile of their family's crash. Emotional beat: fury and hunger—finally, someone asking the right questions.

chapters.title: Lisbon Layover
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Dane and Noor find Mara; she agrees to fly them east only to confront her father herself. Emotional beat: guarded alliance forming, three strangers bound by one man's secrets.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Vasari's POV flashback chapter. How he spent years copying the Ledger from inside the syndicate, and why he chose a crowded flight as cover—regret for the risk he forced on innocents. Emotional beat: guilt as engine, a moral man doing monstrous things.

chapters.title: Crossing the Corridor
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The cargo flight into Georgia, running dark to avoid syndicate tracking; near-miss with an interceptor. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing under fire—trust earned at 30,000 feet.

chapters.title: Safehouse Static
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. Reunion between Vasari and Mara goes badly; accusations, old wounds. Then the safehouse's radio betrays a tail—they've been tracked since Lisbon. Emotional beat: intimacy failing exactly when survival demands unity.

chapters.title: Twelve Rows Down
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Decoding the Ledger, Noor finds row twelve of their family's flight listed as 'controlled.' Grief detonates into clarity: the crash was a demonstration. Emotional beat: devastation transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. She reveals to her superiors that Vasari was allowed to defect—the whole extraction is a trap to identify every investigator who ever doubted the crashes. Noor's name is already on her list. Emotional beat: the trap closing, elegant and merciless.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Depot
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The handoff at a rail depot becomes a firefight; Dane takes a bullet shielding Vasari. They escape by train, barely. Emotional beat: sacrifice forging the bond words couldn't—blood as proof of belonging.

chapters.title: The Bait Confesses
chapters.summary: Vasari's POV. Vasari admits he suspected he was bait all along and let himself be used, gambling that someone like Noor would come digging. Mara walks out. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness colliding; love tested against deception.

chapters.title: Black Site Bargain
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Captured briefly by Brandt, Noor is offered their family's full crash file in exchange for the Ledger. Noor pretends to consider—buying time, memorizing everything. Emotional beat: temptation met with cold clarity; the price of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Runway Zero
chapters.summary: Dane's POV, wounded. Dane orchestrates the escape plan: Mara's cargo plane, a fogged runway, every asset they have left. Emotional beat: a disgraced man finding redemption in competence, holding the line so others can run.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Climax: instead of fleeing, Noor uploads the Ledger publicly from the plane mid-flight, unmasking the syndicate and the engineered crashes—including row twelve. Brandt's forces scramble; the plane vanishes into the storm. Emotional beat: grief offered to the world, anonymity burned as the final price.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Governments move; Brandt is arrested by her own employers as liability. Vasari surrenders voluntarily to testify, asking Mara only to visit. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, accountability chosen over escape.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Months later, Mara flies Noor and recovering Dane to the memorial site of Flight 447. Vasari writes letters from custody that Mara actually answers. Emotional beat: found family settling into something durable, grief shared instead of hoarded.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Final scene: Noor visits row twelve one last time—not counting, just saying goodbye—then goes home to a quiet apartment where Dane left soup and Mara left a flight schedule. That night, Noor sleeps until morning. Emotional beat: resolution—the price paid, belonging earned, rest finally possible.
